commit 6be3a4a0fe117a16eb01f5bb676be824f7bae57a
ordinal 85
date 2026-08-07 22:53:53 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Remove bad worked example #6 -- a null result, explicitly not a blocklist
Added, measured twice, removed. On a control that demonstrably produces empty
glosses (13.7% of concepts) adding #6 did not reduce them in either run, and the
point estimate moved the wrong way both times. Its own pre-registered falsifier
said revert, so it is reverted.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Every delta was inside the noise band, so nothing was shown to
be harmful; n is 6 clauses on one model at one temperature; and the metric is a
proxy that scores legitimate primitives like system_message as empty. This is a
null result on a weak instrument. The failure mode itself is real and unchanged
-- 10 of 133 concepts, corroborated independently by STEP_stage4.md finding (5).

Matt's condition on the removal, recorded in the decision file: this must not
blocklist the idea. Four named routes back, any one sufficient -- a better
instrument (a seat 4r verdict outranks this null entirely), adequate power (12
rule-positive clauses x 6 repeats, about $0.21), a different form (only one was
tried; the prose-only arm was also inside the band, so neither form was shown to
work NOR ruled out), or a different model. The one thing barred is re-adding it
without a fresh pre-registration because it reads well.

The section 2.2 ruling is untouched: failure mode #4 remains restored as a
documented failure mode, and stage 4 seat 4r remains where detection lives.

352 tests pass; translate.py --self-test 52 passed / 1 failed, the pre-existing
stale dryrun.txt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 491cadbad8c04e9b64a833a19d2f4b7cfba5a317
ordinal 89
date 2026-08-07 23:22:32 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject stage 4: the read-back renderer — total layer 1, fluent layer 2, RB1-RB5
A validated schema.Module into English, deterministically, before any seat
runs. Two layers, and which one produced a rendering is recorded and printed.

Layer 1 is TOTAL and that is the point (STEP_stage4 section 2, Matt's ruling):
no ASP construct may be inadmissible. It walks the rule with clingo.ast, takes
str(node), and substitutes glosses — no node-type introspection, so there is no
node type it can refuse. Choice aggregates, pooling, #false and bodies clingo
cannot even parse all render. Restricting the ASP to suit the renderer would
move the problem out of view.

Layer 2 templates: symbolic atoms, negation, comparisons, #count/#sum/#min/#max,
conditional literals, and the five item shapes of 2.3. Polarity comes from
Literal.sign, never from prose — 2.2's recorded killer.

A MISSING GLOSS IS NOT A MISSING TEMPLATE. An earlier draft let an unglossed
atom fall back to layer 1, which reported 10 of 106 real items as unsupported
ASP when every one was an ordinary unary atom nobody had written a meaning for.
Unglossed names now render as a marked hole at layer 2 and raise
readback-ungloss, which blocks the clause from every seat — it fires on m0053's
interactable_entity today, as 2.3 predicted.

RB1-RB5 as specified. RB4 is reported and stamps non-evidential; it never fails
a clause, because a threshold on an echo score is the scoring instrument open
question 3 forbids.

Two places the plan could not be executed as written, both reported rather than
papered over: 2.3's act/1 template needs a gloss no schema field holds and no
module supplies, so the act term is rendered as itself, marked, and noted (RB1
exempts the marked span by name); and RB1 as literally specified fires on
ordinary English nouns inside a gloss, so each finding now says whether the
label sat in the gloss or in the renderer's own text — 18 and 16 respectively on
the corpus, and collapsing them would misdirect every repair.

19/19 hand-written mutants killed. Suite 467 pass, none lost.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 67f0903872991038bf3cb76e6a5126e61ca8b514
ordinal 76
date 2026-08-07 19:59:41 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject guard: all six watched files reviewed and accepted -- green for the first time
Matt re-reviewed the review queue and accepted all six by name: the design doc
and the five transcriptions of it (four prompt files and schema.py). The
staleness guard now reports every watched file at its recorded review point, so
the pre-commit hook stops blocking and this is the first commit that does not
need --no-verify.

Accepting is per file and there is deliberately no accept-all, so this is six
separate recorded human acts, not one.

ONE TEST HAD TO CHANGE, and for the reason DEBUGGING_TIPS.md entry 9 names.
test_pre_commit_fires_when_a_watched_file_is_staged asserted returncode == 1
with the comment "schema.py has never been reviewed, so this must also BLOCK".
The moment schema.py was legitimately reviewed the test failed and reported a
completed review as a defect -- the third instance in this repo of pinning a
live value in a test.

Split into two: one asserts the hook fires at all, and a new one asserts the
contract that actually holds in both states -- the hook blocks EXACTLY when the
guard is unhappy. Verified in both directions: with the guard green it passes and
requires exit 0, and with a digest deliberately corrupted the guard goes to exit
1 and the test then requires the hook to block.

Still open and NOT resolved by this commit: the world-fact question. The design
cites m0255's protects_third_party as the exemplary world fact at 03_pipeline.md
line 119, and its own line 132 says the three licence classes do not reach the
behaviour side -- and that fact lives in behaviour_harm3p.lp. The prompt does not
carry the example, so the contradiction is confined to the design document.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----
